questions.question: Mini-quiz: classify each as Power Query, Power Pivot (Data Model) or Power BI. (a) Removing the Total row and fixing dates in a timesheet CSV. (b) Writing the measure Total Cost := [Labour Cost] + [PO Cost]. (c) A report page with slicers that you publish so the FD can open it in a browser. (d) Unpivoting the Jan-26...Dec-26 budget columns. (e) Relating Projects to Timesheets so one slicer filters both.
questions.answer: (a) Power Query. (b) Power Pivot / Data Model (DAX) - and the same engine inside Power BI. (c) Power BI (report + Service). (d) Power Query. (e) Power Pivot / Data Model (relationships) - Power BI has the identical Model view.
questions.definition: Power Query = get and shape (M, one table at a time, runs at refresh). Power Pivot = the Data Model inside Excel: VertiPaq in-memory columnar tables, relationships, DAX measures. Power BI Desktop = Power Query + the same Data Model + visuals; the Power BI Service adds sharing, scheduled refresh and dashboards. Same engines, three places to use them.
questions.how: Ask: is it changing the shape/content of ONE table before loading (PQ), relating tables or calculating on filtered data (Model/DAX), or presenting/sharing (report/Service)?
questions.answer_text: (a) Power Query. (b) Power Pivot / Data Model (DAX) - and the same engine inside Power BI. (c) Power BI (report + Service). (d) Power Query. (e) Power Pivot / Data Model (relationships) - Power BI has the identical Model view.

questions.question: JE asks: should Callen-Lenz build ONE big model with everything (labour, purchases, stock, budget, cards, assets) or many small ones? What would you do?
questions.answer: Start with one focused model per business question, built as a star schema: a 'Project Cost' model (labour, purchases, budget, stock valuation) sharing conformed dimensions (Project, Employee, Part, Date). Do not dump everything into one giant model: it is slow to refresh, hard to test and to secure, and every report author sees all the data (cards and payroll-type data need tighter access). Do not build many isolated models either: duplicated logic gives two answers for the same number. Practical route: one certified shared semantic model (dataset) per subject area, published once in the Service; people build thin reports on top of it ('live connection') and reuse the same measures. Add a second model (e.g. Treasury: cards, assets) only when the subject and audience differ.
questions.definition: Rule of thumb: one model per subject area / audience, star schema, shared dimensions, measures defined once. Split when refresh time, security or ownership differ; merge when two reports keep needing the same dimensions and measures.
questions.how: Discussion question; mark on: star schema mentioned, single source of truth, security/audience, refresh cost, avoids duplicate logic.

questions.definition: Period for Q21-Q25: Jan-Jun 2026, i.e. AFTER the June timesheet has been dropped in and refreshed (labour by month of Week Ending; purchases by Order Date; budget by Month). Model: FactLabour (Lab 2 LabourLines, 2,320 rows), FactPurchases (cleaned Purchase Log, 200 cancelled-free lines, Line Value = Qty x Net Unit Price), FactBudget (Lab 5 unpivot, 96 rows), FactStockValuation (Lab 3, 60 parts). PO Cost = sum of Qty x Net Unit Price for Order Date in Jan-Jun 2026 (2025 lines excluded by the date filter).

questions.question: A student adds a slicer on DimEmployee[Employee Name] and a card showing Budget (= SUM(FactBudget[Budget GBP])). Whatever employee they click, the card shows the same number. Why, and what are the choices to fix it?
questions.answer: There is no relationship path from DimEmployee to FactBudget: budget is held by project and month, not by employee. A slicer only filters tables it is related to (DimEmployee -> FactLabour), so FactBudget never receives the filter and the SUM ignores it. Choices: (1) accept it - 'budget has no employee grain'; it is the correct answer, and better to hide/blank the card when an employee is selected, e.g. Budget (safe) = IF(ISFILTERED(DimEmployee), BLANK(), [Budget]); (2) allocate the budget to employees in the model (needs a defined allocation rule, e.g. by hours share) - do not invent one; (3) do NOT 'fix' it with a bi-directional or many-to-many relationship between employee and budget - it hides the problem and gives wrong totals. The same logic explains why PO Cost does not react to a Department slicer: FactPurchases has no employee/department column.
questions.definition: Filters flow from the one side of a relationship to the many side. FactBudget is related to DimProject and DimDate only. A measure over a table with no relationship to the slicer's table is unaffected by it.
questions.how: Model view: check that DimEmployee has no line to FactBudget; test with a table visual of Employee x Budget (identical value on every row).
